key_insight: Staged knowledge distillation lets visual quantum reinforcement learning shift from hard end-to-end pixel training to a compact-head problem that shallow VQC policies can actually learn.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical path for building small quantum-compatible control policies on visual tasks without requiring large, unstable hybrid RL training loops.
method: Train a classical visual teacher on pixel inputs.
Freeze the teacher encoder as a shared feature interface.
Distil the teacher policy into compact downstream heads, either classical or VQC-based, using the same frozen representation.
evidence_signal: The approach was evaluated on CartPole Pixels and Acrobot Pixels, where shallow angle-encoded VQC heads achieved near-teacher behavior and amplitude-encoded heads remained workable but more fragile.
watch_item: Amplitude-encoded VQC heads maximize compactness but appear sensitive to budget limits, with higher fragility and simulation cost than angle encoding.
paper_title: Staged Hybridisation for Visual Quantum Reinforcement Learning via Knowledge Distillation
